mainTopic: Who gets no קנס in the ברייתא (עריות and שניות, ממאנת, איילונית), and which women have טענת בתולים
overview: The גמרא works through a ברייתא that lists girls who get no קנס for rape or seduction. First it explains the words עריות and שניות there. In one version the line is drawn at כרת, following שמעון התימני. In another version it is drawn at לאוין, following רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. Next the גמרא notices that the ממאנת line seems to follow the רבנן, while the איילונית line seems to follow רבי מאיר. It tries several ways to fit the whole ברייתא to one opinion, and settles on an unnamed תנא who agrees with רבי מאיר on one point and disagrees on another. רפרם's reading of 'ממאנת' is left with a קשיא. Then a different ברייתא is raised about the איילונית, which leads to a clash between two ברייתות over טענת בתולים for a חרשת and a שוטה. רב ששת resolves it as a מחלוקת between רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע, using the rule 'פתח פיך לאלם'. Finally, the גמרא challenges the ruling that a בוגרת has no טענת בתולים, based on רב's ruling that she is given the whole first night.

steps.title: Secondary relatives cannot mean rabbinic relatives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge. If עריות means Torah-level relatives and שניות means rabbinic relatives, why would the שניות get no קנס? By Torah law she is fit to marry him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If 'עריות' means actual Torah-forbidden relatives and 'שניות' means relatives forbidden only by the rabbis, there is a problem. By Torah law she is fit for him, so why would they have no קנס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question about how to read the words עריות and שניות in the ברייתא. It shows that the usual meaning of שניות (rabbinic relatives) cannot work here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually 'שניות' means relatives the rabbis forbade, while עריות are forbidden by the Torah. But the Torah's קנס should apply to any girl the Torah lets him marry. A rabbinic ban should not take away a Torah payment, so listing rabbinic relatives as 'no קנס' makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives with whom relations are forbidden (here, the more severe group)
'Secondary' relatives, usually ones the rabbis forbade
Forbidden by rabbinic law, not Torah law
The fixed fine a rapist or seducer pays the girl's father
She is fit (allowed) for him

phrases.english: [If עריות means] actual forbidden relatives,
and 'secondary ones' are [forbidden] by rabbinic law,
since by Torah law she is fit for him,
why do they have no fine?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא חַזְיָא לֵיהּ, אַמַּאי אֵין לָהֶן קְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge that started before this section, on the meaning of the ברייתא's terms.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading שניות in the ברייתא as rabbinically forbidden relatives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah-law קנס should not be taken away because of a rabbinic ban. A woman who is fit for him by Torah law should get the קנס.

steps.title: Forbidden relatives are capital cases and secondary ones are כרת cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the terms. עריות are relatives punished by מיתת בית דין, and שניות are relatives punished by כרת. Relatives forbidden only by a לאו do get a קנס, so the ברייתא follows שמעון התימני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'עריות' are those punished by court death, and 'שניות' are those punished by כרת. But those forbidden by a plain לאו do have a קנס. Whose view is this? It is שמעון התימני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the two words new meanings that fit the ברייתא. It then names the תנא who holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both groups, מיתות בית דין and כריתות, are relationships where קידושין do not take effect. A girl in a לאו relationship can be married to him, so she gets a קנס. That matches שמעון התימני, who denies the קנס only where קידושין cannot work.

keyTerms.meaning: Sins punished by the court with death
Sins punished by כרת (spiritual cutting off)
Sins that break a regular negative commandment
Whose [opinion] is it?

phrases.english: Rather: 'forbidden relatives' are those liable to court-imposed death,
'secondary ones' are those liable to karet.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין יֵשׁ לָהֶן קְנָס,
phrases.english: But those liable for [regular] prohibitions do have a fine,
and whose [view] is it? It is Shimon HaTimni.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: ״עֲרָיוֹת״ — חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 1 by redefining the terms.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of terms, then naming the matching תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: עריות are מיתות בית דין and שניות are כריתות. לאוין get a קנס, as שמעון התימני holds.

steps.title: A second reading: secondary relatives are plain prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: Another version reads עריות as both מיתות בית דין and כריתות, and שניות as לאוין. In that version the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: 'עריות' are those punished by court death and those punished by כרת, and 'שניות' are those forbidden by a לאו. Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the answer. It moves the line one level down, so even לאו relationships get no קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the girl gets no קנס even in a לאו case, where קידושין would take effect. That is stricter than שמעון התימני, so the ברייתא is given to רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, who holds that view.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: ״עֲרָיוֹת״ — חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין וְחַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת,
phrases.english: 'forbidden relatives' are those liable to court death and those liable to karet,
'secondary ones' are those liable for [regular] prohibitions.

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי — רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא הִיא.
phrases.english: Whose [view] is it? It is Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of עריות and שניות. In the first, the line is drawn at כרת (שמעון התימני). In the second, it is drawn at לאוין (רבי שמעון בן מנסיא).
steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי ״עֲרָיוֹת״ — חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין וְחַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of step 2's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שניות are כריתות, and לאוין get a קנס.
steps.terutzMaskana: עריות are both מיתות בית דין and כריתות, and שניות are לאוין, following רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.

steps.title: From the line about a refusing girl: an ordinary minor gets a fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that a ממאנת gets no קנס and no פיתוי payment. From it the גמרא infers that an ordinary קטנה does get a קנס, which is the view of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ממאנת has neither a rape fine nor a seduction fine. That implies an ordinary minor does have one. Whose view is that? It is the רבנן, who say a minor has a קנס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא and draws an inference from it about an ordinary minor. This sets up the problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממאנת is a girl who was married off as a minor and is still young. She gets no קנס only because she was already married. That suggests a minor who was never married would get a קנס, which matches the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl married off as a minor who refuses (does מיאון) to stay married
Seduction (and the fine paid for it)
A minor girl, before signs of puberty
This implies (an inference from the wording)
The Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: A girl who refuses does not have
either a fine [for rape] or [a fine for] seduction.
This implies an ordinary minor does have [a fine].
Whose [view] is it? It is the Rabbis,
who say: a minor has a fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְמָאֶנֶת אֵין לָהּ לֹא קְנָס וְלֹא פִּיתּוּי. הָא קְטַנָּה בְּעָלְמָא — אִית לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the ממאנת line, an ordinary קטנה gets a קנס, which is the רבנן's view.

steps.title: The next line about an איילונית follows רבי מאיר instead
steps.stepSummary: The next line of the ברייתא says an איילונית gets no קנס. That fits רבי מאיר, who holds a minor gets no קנס, because she goes straight from minor to בוגרת. So the start of the ברייתא follows the רבנן and the end follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the later line: an איילונית has neither a rape fine nor a seduction fine. Now we have come to רבי מאיר, who says a minor has no קנס, and she went straight from being a minor to being a בוגרת. So the first part is the רבנן and the last part is רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the ברייתא follows the רבנן. It points out that the very next line seems to follow רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איילונית never shows signs of puberty, so she counts as a minor until she becomes a בוגרת. She is never a נערה, the only stage when a קנס applies according to רבי מאיר. If the ברייתא gave a קנס to minors, she should get one, so it seems to be רבי מאיר, and the ברייתא is split.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the last part
A woman who does not develop normal signs of puberty
Full adulthood (the stage of a בוגרת)
The first part

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: אַיְילוֹנִית אֵין לָהּ לֹא קְנָס וְלֹא פִּיתּוּי.
phrases.english: An aylonit has neither a fine [for rape] nor [a fine for] seduction.
We have come to Rabbi Meir,
who said: a minor does not have a fine,
and this one went out from her minority to adulthood.
phrases.notes: He means she skipped the in-between stage of being a נערה, which is when the fine applies.

phrases.english: The first clause is the Rabbis and the latter clause is Rabbi Meir!

steps.confusionAlert: For רבי מאיר, the איילונית gets no קנס because she counts as a קטנה, and a קטנה gets no קנס. She then goes straight to being a בוגרת, so she never reaches the נערה stage when a קנס would apply.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: אַיְילוֹנִית אֵין לָהּ לֹא קְנָס וְלֹא פִּיתּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 4's conclusion that the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The איילונית line only makes sense according to רבי מאיר. A single ברייתא should not switch between opinions.

steps.title: Suggestion: it is all רבי מאיר, and he agrees with רבי יהודה on refusal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the whole ברייתא is רבי מאיר. On the question of a ממאנת, he would hold like רבי יהודה, so the ממאנת in the ברייתא is a נערה, not a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the whole ברייתא is רבי מאיר, and about a ממאנת he holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts forward a possible answer to remove the split. It does this only so it can test the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה lets a girl do מיאון even as a נערה. If רבי מאיר agreed, the ממאנת line would be about a נערה. Then it would say nothing about ordinary minors, and the whole ברייתא could be רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a suggested answer)
All of it
He holds like

phrases.english: And if you will say:
the whole [ברייתא] is Rabbi Meir,
and regarding a refusing girl he holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 5's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the whole ברייתא one opinion by giving רבי מאיר a different view on מיאון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is split between the רבנן and רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested: everything is רבי מאיר, and the ממאנת is a נערה, following רבי יהודה's view of מיאון.

steps.title: Rejected: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about refusal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר really holds like רבי יהודה. A ברייתא shows he does not: רבי מאיר allows מיאון only until two hairs appear, while רבי יהודה allows it until the black hair is greater than the white skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does he hold that? Isn't it taught: until when may a girl refuse? Until she brings two hairs. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: until the black is more than the white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggested answer from step 6. It quotes a ברייתא that shows the two תנאים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two hairs mark the start of being a נערה, so for רבי מאיר a ממאנת is always a minor. Only רבי יהודה lets a נערה do מיאון. So רבי מאיר cannot be holding like רבי יהודה, and the problem from step 5 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But does he really hold that?
Two hairs, the sign that a girl has become a נערה
When the black (hair) is more than the white (skin), a sign of becoming a בוגרת

phrases.english: But does he hold that?
But isn't it taught:
Until when may a girl refuse?
Until she brings two hairs,
the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
until the black is more than the white.
phrases.notes: The black is the pubic hair and the white is the skin. This is the sign that she has become a בוגרת.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, מיאון stops at two hairs, so a ממאנת is always a minor. Only רבי יהודה extends מיאון into the נערה years. That is why the suggestion in step 6 fails.
steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לַהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא: עַד מָתַי הַבַּת מְמָאֶנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 6's suggested answer using a ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי מאיר holds like רבי יהודה regarding מיאון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא records an explicit disagreement: רבי מאיר ends מיאון at two hairs, so he never allows a נערה to do מיאון.

steps.title: New suggestion: the ברייתא is רבי יהודה, who agrees with רבי מאיר about a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now says the whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. On the question of a minor's קנס, though, he holds like רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and about a minor girl he holds like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The last attempt failed, so the גמרא tries a new author for the whole ברייתא: רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows מיאון even for a נערה, so the ממאנת in the ברייתא can be a נערה. On whether a minor gets a קנס, he agrees with רבי מאיר that she does not, so the איילונית line also fits. Now one author covers both lines of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the גמרא drops the last answer and offers a new one.
A girl under twelve.
He holds like (another חכם's view).

phrases.english: Rather: it is רבי יהודה,
and about a minor girl he holds like רבי מאיר.
phrases.notes: He means רבי מאיר's view that a minor gets no קנס. That is what makes the איילונית line work.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 showed that רבי מאיר does not hold like רבי יהודה, the גמרא flips it around: the author is רבי יהודה, who holds like רבי מאיר on one point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-assigning the author of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed split: the start followed the רבנן and the end followed רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא is רבי יהודה, who allows מיאון for a נערה and agrees that a minor gets no קנס.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really agree that a minor gets no קנס?
steps.stepSummary: רב said only 'this is the statement of רבי מאיר'. If רבי יהודה agreed, רב should have named both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really hold that? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: 'This is the statement of רבי מאיר.' If רבי יהודה agreed, רב should have said: 'This is the statement of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי מאיר about a minor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב named only רבי מאיר as holding that a minor gets no קנס. If רבי יהודה held the same, רב would have named him too. So it looks like רבי יהודה does not hold this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he really hold that? It opens a challenge.
And if it were so.
He should have said.

phrases.english: And does he hold that?
But didn't רב יהודה say that רב said:
This is the statement of רבי מאיר.
phrases.notes: This refers to a later משנה, which says a girl who can still be sold by her father, meaning a minor, gets no קנס.

phrases.english: And if it were so,

phrases.aramaic: ״זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: he should have said: 'This is the statement of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לַהּ? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 8's claim that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי מאיר about a minor.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds a minor gets no קנס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב named only רבי מאיר. If רבי יהודה agreed, his name would have been added.

steps.title: This תנא agrees with רבי מאיר on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: The author is an unnamed תנא, not רבי יהודה himself. He agrees with רבי מאיר that a minor gets no קנס, but disagrees about מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא holds like רבי מאיר on one point and disagrees with him on one point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows a תנא who mixes the views: he agrees with רבי מאיר on one point and not on the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the author is not רבי יהודה himself, רב did not need to name him. This תנא agrees with רבי מאיר that a minor gets no קנס. Like רבי יהודה, he lets a נערה do מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: A חכם of the משנה period, or here the unnamed author of a ברייתא.
In one point.
He disagrees with him.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא can be read as the work of one תנא who agrees with רבי מאיר about a minor's קנס but disagrees with him about how long מיאון is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: This תנא holds like רבי מאיר on one point,
and disagrees with him on one point.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by saying the author is an unnamed תנא, not רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying an unnamed תנא with a mixed position
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The author was רבי יהודה, so רב should have named him.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unnamed תנא holds like רבי מאיר about a minor's קנס and against him about מיאון.

steps.title: רפרם: 'ממאנת' means a girl who is able to do מיאון
steps.stepSummary: רפרם reads 'ממאנת' as any girl who is young enough to do מיאון, meaning a minor. Then the whole ברייתא is רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said: What does 'a girl who refuses' mean? A girl who is fit to refuse.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם gives a different way to make the whole ברייתא follow רבי מאיר, by reading the word 'ממאנת' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ממאנת' does not mean a girl who actually did מיאון. It means any girl still young enough to do it, which is a minor. Since רבי מאיר holds a minor gets no קנס, both lines of the ברייתא now fit רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who refuses (does מיאון).
A girl who is fit (old enough or young enough) to refuse.

phrases.english: רפרם said:
What does 'a girl who refuses' mean?
One who is fit to refuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַפְרָם אָמַר: מַאי ״מְמָאֶנֶת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, separate answer to the contradiction from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ממאנת' meant a girl who actually refused.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means any minor who could refuse, so the whole ברייתא is רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Then why not just say 'a minor'? Left as a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: If 'ממאנת' just means a minor, the ברייתא should have said 'a minor'. The גמרא leaves this as an unanswered קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it teach 'a minor'! It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רפרם: why use the roundabout word 'ממאנת' if it simply means a minor? It has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would normally use the simple word 'קטנה'. Since רפרם's reading makes the wording strange, the גמרא leaves his answer standing with a question on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it teach.
It is difficult. The challenge stays unanswered.

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' here does not mean the whole sugya falls apart. It only means רפרם's reading has a problem that the גמרא does not answer.

phrases.english: Then let it teach 'a minor'!
It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיתְנֵי קְטַנָּה! קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רפרם's reading from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רפרם's reading of 'ממאנת' as 'a girl fit to refuse'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא meant a minor, it would have said so plainly.

steps.title: The ברייתא's line: an איילונית gets no קנס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next line of the ברייתא: an איילונית gets no קנס and no פיתוי payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: An איילונית has neither a fine for rape nor a payment for seduction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the איילונית line again to set up a new question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, this line was used to figure out who wrote the ברייתא. Now the גמרא is about to test it against another ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who never develops the signs of maturity and cannot have children.
The fixed fine paid for raping a נערה.
Seduction, which also carries a fixed payment.

phrases.english: An איילונית has
neither a fine for rape nor a payment for seduction.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְילוֹנִית אֵין לָהּ לֹא קְנָס וְלֹא פִּיתּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ממאנת discussion to a new look at the איילונית line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An איילונית receives neither קנס nor פיתוי payment.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says an איילונית does get a קנס
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא says a deaf woman, a mentally incompetent woman and an איילונית do get a קנס and are subject to טענת בתולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא contrasts it with another ברייתא: A deaf woman, a mentally incompetent woman and an איילונית have a fine, and they have a claim of virginity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction: another ברייתא gives an איילונית a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא says an איילונית gets no קנס, but this one says she does. It also says these women are subject to טענת בתולים, meaning the husband can claim she was not a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it. This introduces a contradicting source.
A deaf woman who cannot speak.
A mentally incompetent woman.
The husband's claim that his bride was not a בתולה.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it:
A deaf woman, a mentally incompetent woman, and an איילונית:
they have a fine,
and they have a claim of virginity.
phrases.notes: If her husband finds she was not a בתולה, he can make her lose her כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי: הַחֵרֶשֶׁת וְהַשּׁוֹטָה וְהָאַיְילוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the איילונית line quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an איילונית gets no קנס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא says outright that an איילונית does get a קנס.

steps.title: No real contradiction: one is רבי מאיר, the other is the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two ברייתות simply follow two different views: ours is רבי מאיר and the other is the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what contradiction is this? This one is רבי מאיר, and that one is the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא waves away the contradiction as an obvious מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that רבי מאיר gives no קנס to an איילונית and the רבנן do. So two ברייתות that disagree just match the two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: A contradiction.
The majority of חכמים who disagree with רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: And this, what contradiction is it?
This one is רבי מאיר,
that one is the רבנן!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא, מַאי רוּמְיָא? הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole contradiction about the איילונית's קנס
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two ברייתות simply follow the known מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and the רבנן.

steps.title: So why was the contradiction raised at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the answer is so obvious, why did the person bother to raise the contradiction?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who raised it, why did he raise it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders why anyone raised such an easy contradiction. This sets up the real reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and the רבנן is well known. So the person must have had a deeper reason for quoting this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises it, meaning he poses the contradiction.

phrases.english: And the one who raised it,
why did he raise it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָאָרֵי לַהּ, מַאי קָאָרֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why step 14 was raised, given the easy answer in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the contradiction was raised if its answer is so obvious.

steps.title: He raised it to set up a clash with another ברייתא about טענת בתולים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא was quoted because another ברייתא clashes with it. That one says a deaf woman and a mentally incompetent woman have no טענת בתולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he has another ברייתא to contrast with it: A deaf woman, a mentally incompetent woman, a בוגרת, and a woman whose hymen was torn by an object have no claim of virginity. A blind woman and an איילונית do have a claim of virginity. סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר: A blind woman has no claim of virginity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real reason for quoting the ברייתא: it clashes with yet another ברייתא, and that clash is not about the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 14 said a deaf woman and a mentally incompetent woman are subject to טענת בתולים. This new ברייתא says they are not. That contradiction cannot be explained away as רבי מאיר against the רבנן, so it was worth raising.

keyTerms.meaning: To contrast, meaning to set up a contradiction.
A girl past twelve and a half, a full adult.
A girl whose hymen was torn by an object or injury, not by relations.
A blind person.

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות agree that an איילונית has טענת בתולים. The clash is about the deaf woman and the mentally incompetent woman.
steps.whatToRemember: The real contradiction is about טענת בתולים for a חרשת and a שוטה, not about the קנס of an איילונית.

phrases.english: Because he has
another one to contrast with it:
A deaf woman and a mentally incompetent woman
and a grown woman and a woman whose hymen was torn by an object:
they have no claim of virginity.
A blind woman and an איילונית:
they have a claim of virginity.
סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר:
A blind woman has no claim of virginity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִית לֵיהּ לְמִירְמֵא אַחֲרִיתִי עִילָּוֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 and sets up a new contradiction against the ברייתא of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first ברייתא was quoted to set up a contradiction with another ברייתא, which denies טענת בתולים to a חרשת and a שוטה.

steps.title: רב ששת: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the two ברייתות do not really clash. One follows רבן גמליאל and the other follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: There is no difficulty. This ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל, and that ברייתא follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the clash from Step 17. He says each ברייתא matches a different side of an older argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל holds that a woman is believed when she says she lost her virginity after אירוסין, so she keeps her כתובה. Under his view, the ברייתא that says the deaf and incompetent woman have no טענת בתולים makes sense. רבי יהושע says she is not believed, which fits the ברייתא that says they are subject to טענת בתולים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This phrase opens an answer that removes a contradiction.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: It is not difficult:
this one is Rabban Gamliel,
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא that says the deaf and incompetent woman have no טענת בתולים.

phrases.english: and that one is Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings on the very same women.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect the argument between רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע about whether the woman is believed.

steps.title: Does רבן גמליאל's rule help a woman who cannot make the claim?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. רבן גמליאל believes a woman who makes the claim herself, but a deaf or incompetent woman cannot make any claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that you heard רבן גמליאל believes her where she herself makes the claim. Where she does not make the claim, did you hear that he believes her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's answer. It points out that the deaf and incompetent woman never actually say anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's ruling was about a woman who speaks up and says she lost her virginity after the betrothal. A deaf or incompetent woman cannot make that claim. So how can רבן גמליאל's view explain a ברייתא that protects her?

keyTerms.meaning: Say that you heard him. This phrase grants part of an idea in order to question how far it goes.
She claims, meaning she argues her case herself.
Did you hear him say that? This asks for proof that the rule stretches further.

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabban Gamliel rule this way
where she herself makes the claim;
where she herself does not make the claim,
did you hear him say so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the ברייתא freeing the deaf and incompetent woman from טענת בתולים follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל only believed a woman who actively makes a claim. These women cannot make one, so his view may not apply to them.

steps.title: Yes, the court speaks up for her
steps.stepSummary: Yes, רבן גמליאל's view applies to her too. If a woman who speaks up is believed, then the court makes the claim for a woman who cannot speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Since רבן גמליאל said she is believed, a case like this falls under 'Open your mouth for the mute.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. Even a woman who cannot speak is protected, because the court makes her claim for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל holds that the claim of being harmed after the betrothal is a believable claim. Once that is so, it would be unfair to let her lose just because she cannot say it. The פסוק 'פתח פיך לאלם' teaches that the court argues on behalf of someone who cannot argue for themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes.
She is believed.
Open your mouth for the mute. The court makes claims for someone who cannot.

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות follow רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע. Under רבן גמליאל, the court makes the claim for a deaf or incompetent woman: 'פתח פיך לאלם'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea in דיני ממונות: when a person cannot argue for themselves, the court raises the arguments they would have made.

phrases.aramaic: אִין, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מְהֵימְנָא,
phrases.english: Yes, since Rabban Gamliel said she is believed,
a case like this is: “Open your mouth for the mute.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מְהֵימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 19 and closes this branch.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the rule through a general principle (פתח פיך לאלם)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל only helps a woman who makes the claim herself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the claim is believable, the court makes it for a woman who cannot speak for herself.

steps.title: Next line: a בוגרת has no טענת בתולים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the step 17 ברייתא saying that a woman who has reached full maturity is not subject to טענת בתולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא said: A בוגרת has no טענת בתולים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא about טענת בתולים from step 17 and quotes its line about a בוגרת. It is setting up a challenge to this line in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בוגרת is a girl who has passed נערות and reached full adulthood. The ברייתא says her husband cannot complain that he did not find her a virgin. The reason assumed is that her body has matured, so signs of virginity may no longer show.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who has reached full maturity, past the stage of נערה.

phrases.english: And a grown woman has no claim concerning virginity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַבּוֹגֶרֶת אֵין לָהּ טַעֲנַת בְּתוּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It goes back to the ברייתא about טענת בתולים quoted in Step 17 and takes up its line about a בוגרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בוגרת is not subject to טענת בתולים.

steps.title: Challenge from רב: a בוגרת gets the whole first night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from רב's ruling. A בוגרת is given the whole first night, which suggests she does have signs of virginity.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say: A בוגרת is given the whole first night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the line it just quoted. It uses a ruling of רב that seems to assume a בוגרת still has her virginity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב rules that for a בוגרת, any blood seen during the whole first night is treated as the blood of virginity, not נדה blood. That only makes sense if she still has signs of virginity. If so, why should she have no טענת בתולים?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't רב say? This opens a challenge from a known ruling.
The first night of the marriage.
We give her, meaning she is allowed this time.

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not talking about money or the כתובה here. He is talking about טהרה, whether blood she sees counts as virginity blood or as נדה. The גמרא uses this to show that a בוגרת still has signs of virginity.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
A grown woman, we give her the first night!
phrases.notes: He means that all blood she sees that whole night is treated as virginity blood, not נדה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב: בּוֹגֶרֶת, נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line of the ברייתא quoted in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a בוגרת has no טענת בתולים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's ruling assumes a בוגרת still has signs of virginity. If so, her husband should be able to make a טענת בתולים.
